Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this. We are finalizing our infra budget and want to understand Redwood Dedicated commit economics for two workload buckets: (1) embedding-heavy production queries (mostly short inputs, high QPS, very tight cost per embedding) and (2) long-form generation for a new assistant product (long contexts, higher memory needs, 99th-percentile tail latency matters).

Specific asks:
- Perf/$ comparatives you recommend for A100/H100/L40S for the two buckets (typical batch sizes: embeddings 32, gen small-batch 1-4).
- Guidance on reserved commit sizing: when is it better to buy pure L40S slabs vs a mixed pool with H100 for peak bursts?
- What throughput guarantees/SLOs look like per tier (e.g., 50k tok/s pooled vs reserved?) and how burst credits work.
- Typical discount bands and commitment lengths for predictable pricing.

We have an internal constraint: can commit to a 12–18 month reserved spend window but need flexibility on GPU mix for first 3 months while we stabilize.

Can you send a short scenarios file (numbers + recommended mixes) and a baseline proposal we can review with finance?

Thanks,

Hi Emma — great summary, thanks. I attached a short scenarios spreadsheet and our most recent latency benchmark PDF (summary below).

Quick preview:
- For embedding-heavy workloads (batch 32): L40S offers the best perf/$ for embeddings (10–18% lower $/embedding vs H100 depending on quantization and model).
- For single-client, long-context generation: H100 gives ~20–25% lower latency for end-to-end generation at comparable quantized configs due to sparsity and tensor-core advantages; A100 lags for very long contexts because of memory pressure.
- Typical approach we recommend: commit to a baseline L40S slab (for steady QPS) + a smaller H100 pool for latency-sensitive tails and model variants. We can operationalize auto-fallback to cheaper L40S variants when H100 capacity is congested.

I'll propose two pricing scenarios and a flexible phase-in (first 90 days we allow swap credits to change GPU mix without penalty). Can we do a 30 minute sync Wednesday? I suggested slots in the attached MAP.

Tessa / Karthik — notes from my cost models and ops constraints:

1) Discount bands (12–18 month commit window)
- 25k USD/mo baseline commit: base discounts ~10% off list for L40S, 8% for H100.
- 50k USD/mo: 15% L40S, 12% H100.
- 150k+ USD/mo: we can push to 22–28% for L40S and 18–22% for H100 depending on GPU mix and guaranteed throughput SLO.

2) Slab vs mixed pool decision matrix (ops perspective)
- If steady-state QPS is predictable (+/- 10%), pure L40S slab is lowest unit cost and simplest to operate.
- If tail latency (99th) for gen matters and you have a non-trivial spike shape (bursts >3x baseline), then a mixed pool with smaller H100 capacity plus burst credits gives better end-user latency and predictable cost. Burst credits: we offer a monthly burst pool (pay-as-you-go hours) that is billed at a premium but capped per contract.

3) Throughput guarantees and measurement
- We define throughput SLO as sustained token/sec per pool measured over 5-minute windows; we commit to a minimum sustained throughput for reserved pools and provide credits if we fail (service credits up to x% of monthly fee).
- Example: a 50 H100 equivalent reserved pool set to the gen profile yields ~120k tokens/sec sustained (model dependent). The same budget in L40S-only slabs yields ~95–110k tokens/sec for embeddings-heavy.

4) Operational concession for phase-in
- Offer: first 90 days: GPU mix swaps allowed up to 30% of committed capacity with no repricing; after 90 days mix changes subject to 30-day notice.

I'll prepare the recommended price ladder and a short justification doc. Tessa — propose we put the 50k/mo baseline scenario in the MAP and offer a staged upgrade to 150k/mo after quarter 1 if metrics hit X, Y.

Subject: Proposal: Dedicated capacity scenarios and HDD (H100+L40S) mix options

Emma — attaching a short proposal pack. TL;DR and recommended next steps below.

TL;DR (recommended starter commit)
- 75k USD/mo for 12 months (commit start): allocate as 70% L40S slabs + 30% H100 reserved pool.
- Pricing: blended discount = ~14% off list (L40S 16% / H100 10%).
- Phase-in flexibility: for the first 90 days you can reassign up to 30% of the committed capacity between L40S and H100 without repricing.
- Burst credits: 1,500 GPU-hours/mo of H100-equivalent burst capacity included; additional burst billed at pay-as-you-go premium with a monthly cap.
- Throughput guarantees: we commit to a minimum sustained throughput of 95k tok/s for the blended pool measured on 5-minute windows. If we miss SLO, service credits up to 5% of the monthly fee apply.

Why this mix?
- L40S gives best-cost baseline for high QPS embeddings and lightweight classifier calls.
- H100 covers long-context gen tails and model variants that need tensor-core perf; having a reserved H100 slice reduces 99th-percentile latency for users.

Attachment summary:
- borealis_dedicated_scenarios_2026.xlsx: three tier scenarios (numbers per month, GPU-equivalent, blended perf/$).
- latency_benchmarks_a100_h100_l40s_8-2026.pdf: our internal microbenchmarks (models: 13B embedding model, 70B generative baseline).
- mutual_action_plan_borealis.docx: proposed milestones (integration, smoke tests, production cutover, billing schedule).

Next steps:
1) Confirm interest in 75k/mo starter commit and RPO (we will draft the amendment).
2) If yes, sign the MAP and we'll schedule a kickoff with infra and CS to finalize model pins and autoscaling thresholds (we recommend a 2-week staging window).
3) We are open to a second conversation with finance to finalize discounting and payment terms; Rafael is available to join.

If you'd like, we can also provide a short playbook on quantization and small-batch tuning that shows how to reduce unit cost by ~8–12% without notable quality loss.
